findings.title: DHF write granularity contradicts turn granularity
findings.location: Section 2, Seam C; Section 6, Glossary -> Turn
findings.evidence: Seam C: "Every terminal lifecycle transition produces a DHF write." Glossary: "Turn: One user utterance + the agent's response, possibly containing 0+ tool calls. Turns are the DHF-entry granularity."
findings.problem: A single turn can contain multiple tool calls and therefore multiple terminal lifecycle transitions, but the glossary says the DHF is keyed at turn granularity. The contract does not define whether writes are per tool call or per turn.
findings.why_it_matters: SPEC-03 and SPEC-04 cannot agree on append semantics, record cardinality, or acceptance tests if the unit of persistence is contradictory.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one canonical persistence unit. If DHF is per turn, define how multiple tool outcomes are aggregated into one append. If DHF is per tool call, update the glossary and viewer contract accordingly.

findings.title: Timeout/quarantine logic does not account for irreversible COM side effects
findings.location: Section 2, Seam B; Section 6, Glossary -> Tool-Call Lifecycle State, Quarantine
findings.evidence: Seam B: "SPEC-02 provides a synchronous method surface; SPEC-03 wraps each call in its own timeout and cancel semantics." Glossary: "Tool-Call Lifecycle State: Sent -> Completed | TimedOut | Cancelled | Abandoned." and "Quarantine: A late message received after a terminal lifecycle state is logged and discarded..."
findings.problem: A synchronous SolidWorks COM call that has already begun execution may mutate the CAD model even if the orchestrator marks it TimedOut or Cancelled. The contract treats late completion as discardable, but it does not define how to reconcile actual model changes after timeout.
findings.why_it_matters: The orchestrator and DHF can record a failed call while SolidWorks has already changed state, breaking audit integrity and causing downstream commands to operate on false assumptions.
findings.proposed_fix: Define cancellation as pre-dispatch only unless the adapter can prove in-flight interruption. Add mandatory post-timeout reconciliation/state refresh rules for any mutating call, or remove timeout/cancel guarantees for in-flight synchronous COM execution.

findings.title: SPEC-05 is both declared to depend on SPEC-04 and forbidden from touching it
findings.location: Section 1, Module Map; Section 2, Seams D and E; Section 5, Review Order
findings.evidence: Module Map: "SPEC-05 ... Depends On SPEC-01, SPEC-03, SPEC-04." Seam D: "The agent never touches the ... DHF. It is a pure consumer of the lifecycle surface." Seam E: "SPEC-05 -> SPEC-04 (indirect via SPEC-03)." Review Order: "SPEC-05 ... depends on SPEC-01, 03, 04."
findings.problem: The contract simultaneously describes SPEC-04 as a direct dependency of SPEC-05 and as an indirect/non-touched dependency. It does not state whether SPEC-05 may compile against SPEC-04 or invoke any read surface from it.
findings.why_it_matters: Architecture tests, review ordering, and module ownership cannot be enforced when a dependency is both allowed and prohibited.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the dependency explicit and singular. Either remove SPEC-04 from SPEC-05 dependencies everywhere, or define the exact allowed SPEC-04 surface and update the seam text to match.

findings.title: The no-DTO-outside-Protocol rule is contradicted by `DhfTurnContext`
findings.evidence: Seam A: "Architecture rule: no DTO types exist outside `BSVoiceCAD.Protocol.*` namespaces." Seam C: "The lifecycle layer emits a `DhfTurnContext` (defined in SPEC-04) and hands it to `DhfLedger.AppendTurnAsync`."
findings.problem: `DhfTurnContext` is a data contract crossing a module boundary, but it is defined outside the protocol namespace even though the document says no DTO types exist outside that namespace.
findings.why_it_matters: Either the rule is overstated or the seam violates it. In both cases, dependency enforcement becomes unreliable and reviewers cannot tell which shared types are permitted.
findings.proposed_fix: Limit the rule to wire DTOs only, or move cross-module contract types like `DhfTurnContext` into an explicitly shared contract module/namespace covered by the rule.

findings.title: DHF session closure omits ungraceful termination paths
findings.evidence: "DHF Session: One row in `dhf.sessions`. Opens on first AddinReadyMessage for a given AddinSessionId. Closes when a different AddinSessionId arrives or on orchestrator shutdown."
findings.problem: The contract defines closure only for clean replacement or clean shutdown. It does not define what happens on add-in crash, SolidWorks exit, orchestrator crash, or transport loss.
findings.why_it_matters: Sessions can remain logically open with no authoritative closure rule, which makes restart behavior, append rules, and audit interpretation undefined.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit stale-session detection and recovery semantics for ungraceful termination, including who closes the session, how timeouts are determined, and how reconnects are reconciled.

findings.title: A stretch feature is treated as a mandatory build-validation dependency
findings.location: Section 3, Mandatory vs Stretch; Section 7, Build-Readiness
findings.evidence: Section 3: "voice ... all stretch." Section 7: "Day-0 validation on SolidWorks 2025 SP3+, Anthropic.SDK, Whisper.net CUDA, Postgres 16"
findings.problem: Voice is explicitly descopable stretch work, but Whisper/CUDA validation is listed as a day-0 implementation blocker.
findings.why_it_matters: This introduces a hidden dependency that can delay mandatory scope and distort planning decisions.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove Whisper.net CUDA from mandatory day-0 validation, or explicitly mark it as conditional only if voice remains in scope.

findings.title: Top-level mandatory acceptance tests are referenced without top-level definitions
findings.location: Section 3, Mandatory vs Stretch; Section 0, Non-goals
findings.evidence: Section 3: "Never descoped: ... ACC-01/02/03/04/08/10/12 acceptance tests." Section 0: "Non-goals for this document: ... test names ... Those live in per-module specs."
findings.problem: The contract makes specific ACC items non-descopable while also excluding test definitions from this document. No cross-reference is provided here for what those IDs mean.
findings.why_it_matters: A top-level scope gate is unusable if the contract that cites it does not identify the underlying pass/fail criteria.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a canonical reference for each ACC ID or replace the IDs here with named capabilities that are meaningful at top level.

findings.title: The claimed "model-level consensus mechanism" has no observable contract
findings.evidence: "Opus 4.7's internal self-verification at xhigh effort is the model-level consensus mechanism"
findings.problem: The document claims a consensus mechanism but does not define any observable inputs, outputs, logs, or failure criteria for it.
findings.why_it_matters: Reviewers cannot verify when consensus was invoked, whether it succeeded, or how it should affect ambiguity handling and DHF records.
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove the consensus claim and treat the design as single-model inference, or define an explicit validation contract with measurable outputs and required DHF logging.

top_3_must_fix: Resolve the contradiction between per-turn DHF granularity and "every terminal lifecycle transition produces a DHF write."
Define how timeout/cancel semantics work for synchronous mutating SolidWorks COM calls without corrupting CAD state or DHF truth.
Eliminate the SPEC-05/SPEC-04 dependency contradiction and state one enforceable module boundary.
